takeaway: The thoracic duct runs between the thoracic aorta (lateral to it) and the azygous vein (medial), so it lies lateral to the azygous vein; injury causes chylothorax.

lines.text: Creamy chest drain fluid after oesophagectomy suggests thoracic duct injury. The duct lies lateral to which structure?
The thoracic duct rises from the chyle cisterns in the abdomen, through the aortic hiatus at T12.
lines.say: The thoracic duct rises from the chyle cisterns in the abdomen, through the aortic hiatus at T twelve.

lines.text: In the chest it runs between two neighbours: the thoracic aorta lateral to it, and the azygous vein medially.
So the duct lies lateral to the azygous vein: that is the answer.
The duct is thin-walled and easily missed; if torn, chyle can form a chylothorax.
lines.say: (sigh) The duct is thin-walled and easily missed; if torn, chyle can form a chylothorax.

lines.text: Remember: lateral to the azygous vein.
